encounters.cc: Admitted to intensive care unit for management of septic shock secondary to pneumonia with high urine output

lines: Admitted to intensive care unit for management of septic shock secondary to pneumonia with high urine output

The patient is a 59-year-old male with chronic hepatitis C cirrhosis complicated by hepatocellular carcinoma and status post recent orthotopic liver transplantation who presents to the intensive care unit.
He has a prior history of calcineurin inhibitor nephrotoxicity and perforated peptic ulcer disease.
He initially required high-volume intravenous fluids and broad-spectrum antibiotics.
Over the next two days, his blood pressure remained low despite aggressive fluid resuscitation, and he became progressively lethargic and confused.
Vasopressor therapy with norepinephrine was started but his urine output remained elevated at over 4 liters per day despite worsening hypotension.
Therefore, vasopressin infusion was added to his regimen.
Twelve hours later, nursing staff note that his urine output has significantly decreased, and he appears less thirsty.
He is receiving enteral nutrition and electrolyte repletion as needed.
